nodes.description: HER performance evaluation in 1 M KOH using three-electrode setup (LSV)
nodes.source_text: Figure 3a and S19 show the linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves in 1M KOH. Rh@Dy-CuO exhibits the highest HER activity among the tested catalysts with ultralow overpotentials of 20 and 81 mV at current densities of 10 and 100 mA cm⁻², respectively... It exhibits j₀ = 5.5 mA cm⁻² and a Tafel slope of 33 mV dec⁻¹... Rh@Dy-CuO exhibits an Eₐ of 17.68 kJ mol⁻¹... The ECSA_Rh values of Rh@Dy-CuO... were determined to be 308 m² g_Rh⁻¹... mass activity (648 mA mg_Rh⁻¹)... chronoamperometry tests show that Rh@Dy-CuO maintains nearly constant activity during continuous operation at about -100 mA cm⁻² for 200 h

nodes.description: AEMWE full cell performance with RuO2 as OER counter electrode
nodes.source_text: The Rh@Dy-CuO || RuO₂ electrolyzer achieves 500 mA cm⁻² and 1.0 A cm⁻² at cell voltages of 1.74 and 1.91 V, respectively... The produced H₂ output closely matches the theoretical value, confirming a Faradaic efficiency near 100%... the Rh@Dy-CuO || RuO₂ electrolyzer can operate continuously at 1.0 A cm⁻² for 1000 h without performance decay

nodes.characterization_summary: Rh@Dy-CuO exhibits nanowire morphology retained after alkaline etching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images (Figure 1a and S3) show that Rh@Dy-CuO exhibits a nanowire morphology, which is retained after alkaline etching (Figure S4-S6).

properties.description: Scanning Electron Microscopy image showing nanofiber morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: Rh@Dy-CuO nanowires possess average diameter of ~150 nm with rough surface layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image further shows that the nanowires possess an average diameter of ~150 nm with a rough surface layer (Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: CuO (111) and CuO (002) planes with lattice fringes of 0.232 nm and 0.253 nm confirmed in Rh@Dy-CuO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) and inverse fast Fourier transform (FFT) images confirm the presence of CuO (111) and CuO (002) planes with lattice fringes of 0.232 and 0.253 nm, respectively (Figure S8).

nodes.characterization_summary: Rh@Dy-CuO shows micromesoporous surface, well-defined CuO (111) lattices, Rh and Dy atoms visible as bright spots, Rh mainly as nanoclusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected high angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC HAADF-STEM) image also shows a micromesoporous surface structure... Atomic intensity profiling, 3D topographic imaging, and AC HAADF-STEM image reveal that Rh mainly exists in the form of nanoclusters.

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous distribution of Cu, Dy and Rh confirmed in Rh@Dy-CuO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping further confirms the homogeneous distribution of Cu, Dy and Rh (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized XANES spectra at Rh K-edge show Rh@Dy-CuO absorption edge between Rh foil and Rh₂O₃ but closer to Rh foil, indicating metallic Rh⁰ with slight oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The normalized X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra at the Rh K-edge show that the absorption edge of Rh@Dy-CuO lies between that of Rh foil and Rh₂O₃ but closer to Rh foil, suggesting that Rh predominantly exists in the metallic Rh⁰ state with slight oxidation (Figure 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS and WT-EXAFS at Rh K-edge reveal prominent Rh-O and Rh-Rh bonds with no Rh-O-Rh signal; fitting gives Rh-Rh coordination number 2.6 and Rh-O coordination number 5.0.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) and wavelet transform (WT)-EXAFS spectra reveal prominent Rh-O and Rh-Rh bond, with no detectable Rh-O-Rh signal... FT-EXAFS fitting gives an Rh-Rh coordination number of 2.6 and an Rh-O coordination number of 5.0 (Figure S14a and Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Dy L₃-edge XANES shows Rh@Dy-CuO white-line position lower than Dy₂O₃ (valence < +3) with higher intensity indicating greater 4f orbital occupancy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Dy L₃-edge XANES spectra show that the white-line position of Rh@Dy-CuO is lower than that of Dy₂O₃, indicating an average Dy valence state below +3... The higher white-line intensity of Rh@Dy-CuO compared with Dy₂O₃ suggests greater occupancy of Dy 4f orbitals.

nodes.characterization_summary: Dy L₃-edge FT-EXAFS shows pronounced Dy-O bond, no Dy-Dy bond; Dy-O coordination number slightly lower than Dy₂O₃ confirming atomic dispersion of Dy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FT-EXAFS spectrum of the Dy L₃-edge for Rh@Dy-CuO shows a pronounced Dy-O bond and no Dy-Dy bond... The Dy-O coordination number is slightly lower than in Dy₂O₃, confirming atomic dispersion of Dy within the CuO lattice.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples show Cu (PDF#04-0836) from CF substrate and CuO (PDF#45-0937); Rh@Dy-CuO, Rh@CuO, Dy-CuO CuO peaks shift to higher angles indicating lattice distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns reveal peaks corresponding to Cu (PDF#04-0836) from the CF substrate and CuO (PDF#45-0937) in all samples... indicating lattice distortion induced by Rh/Dy incorporation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu K-edge XANES shows Rh@Dy-CuO absorption edge closer to CuO than Rh@CuO; average Cu oxidation states estimated as +1.70 (Rh@Dy-CuO) and +1.48 (Rh@CuO).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cu K-edge XANES spectra show that the absorption edge of Rh@Dy-CuO is closer to CuO than Rh@CuO, suggesting that Cu in Rh@Dy-CuO retains a higher oxidation state... Taking Cu foil and CuO as references, the average oxidation state of Cu in Rh@Dy-CuO and Rh@CuO is estimated to be +1.70 and +1.48, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu K-edge FT-EXAFS and WT-EXAFS show Rh@Dy-CuO has stronger Cu-O coordination than Rh@CuO; Cu-O bond length 1.93 Å (Rh@Dy-CuO) vs 1.97 Å (Rh@CuO).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with Rh@CuO, Rh@Dy-CuO exhibits stronger Cu-O coordination in both FT-EXAFS and WT-EXAFS spectra... The Cu-O bond length in Rh@Dy-CuO (1.93 Å) is shorter than that in Rh@CuO (1.97 Å).

nodes.characterization_summary: Rh@Dy-CuO Cu 2p shows Cu⁰/¹⁺/Cu²⁺ ratio 0.29 vs 0.32 in Rh@CuO; O1s M-O component 21.4% in Rh@Dy-CuO vs 19.8% in Rh@CuO; Rh 3d peaks shift to lower binding energies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cu 2p spectrum of Rh@CuO exhibits four peaks at 932.9, 934.9, 952.8 and 954.7 eV... Rh@Dy-CuO exhibits a lower Cu⁰/¹⁺/Cu²⁺ ratio of 0.29 compared to that of Rh@CuO (0.32)... The relative contribution of the M-O component in Rh@Dy-CuO (21.4%) is higher than that in Rh@CuO (19.8%).
